sentences.en: I mean, the key problem she faces is that Darnley remains a complete nightmare.
sentences.zh: 他们去了边境中心一个叫做特拉克尔宅邸的地方，那里是一个非常著名的狩猎场。

sentences.en: You know, he's a massive loose cannon.
sentences.zh: 但结果却是一场灾难，因为实际上鹿正在消失。

sentences.en: And also in his personal behaviour, he's terrible.
sentences.zh: 树林开始被砍伐。

sentences.en: He is very, very disrespectful to her.
sentences.zh: 根本没有足够的猎物让达恩利好好享受打猎的乐趣。

sentences.en: Just a kind of awful person.
sentences.zh: 他对此非常生气。

sentences.en: So an example of this is that in August, so by now Mary has recovered from childbirth, she and Darnley, they want to go hunting.
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上，他喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: And they go to a place called Tracker House in the border's centre of very famous hunting ground.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他总是喝醉，但这次他醉得非常厉害。

sentences.en: But it turns out to be a disaster because actually the deer are vanishing.
sentences.zh: 他靠向玛丽说，我们明天要去该死的——你知道的，我们要去打鹿，你他妈的也得跟我们一起去，对吧？

sentences.en: The woods are starting to be chopped down.
sentences.zh: 玛丽不想去。

sentences.en: There isn't enough for Darnley to enjoy a good hunt.
sentences.zh: 她在他的耳边低声说出了一个惊人的消息。

sentences.en: And he gets very cross about this.
sentences.zh: 她说她觉得自己可能又怀孕了。

sentences.en: And one night he just gets spectacularly drunk.
sentences.zh: 而达恩利根本不在乎。

sentences.en: I mean, he's always drunk, but this time he's really badly drunk.
sentences.zh: 他在大厅里把这件事公之于众。

sentences.en: And he leans over to Mary and says, we're going to go bloody, you know, we're going to go hunt deer tomorrow and you're bloody well going to come, right?
sentences.zh: 他说，没关系，如果这个没了，我们还可以再生一个。

sentences.en: And Mary doesn't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 特拉克尔的领主、也就是东道主对此感到震惊，并斥责了他，告诉他说话不像个基督徒。

sentences.en: And she whispers in his ear dramatic news.
sentences.zh: 然后她在他耳边低语了一个爆炸性的消息。

sentences.en: She says she thinks that she may be pregnant again.
sentences.zh: 她说她觉得自己可能又怀孕了。

sentences.en: And Darnley doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 而达恩利根本不在乎。

sentences.en: He reveals this to everyone in the hall.
sentences.zh: 他在大厅里把这件事向所有人公之于众。

sentences.en: He says, nevermind, if we lose this one, we shall make another.
sentences.zh: 他说，没关系，如果我们失去这一个，我们还可以再生一个。

sentences.en: And the Lord of Tracker, his host, is appalled by this and rebukes him and tells him that he doesn't talk like a Christian.
sentences.zh: 而他的主人特拉克勋爵对此感到震惊，并斥责了他，告诉他他的言谈不像一个基督徒。

sentences.en: And Darnley, he snaps his fingers in Lord Tracker's face.
sentences.zh: 而达利居然直接在特拉克尔勋爵的脸上打了个响指。

sentences.en: What are we not to work a mare well when she is with foe?
sentences.zh: 难道母马怀有小马时，我们就不能好好使唤它吗？

sentences.en: And this goes down like a lead balloon with Lord Tracker, with Mary's attendants and with Mary herself.
sentences.zh: 这让特拉克尔勋爵、玛丽的随从以及玛丽本人都感到极为反感。

sentences.en: And she seems to have been so offended by this that she breaks the holiday off and leaves early.
sentences.zh: 她似乎对此感到十分恼火，以至于中断了假期并提前离开。

sentences.en: She's quite right.
sentences.zh: 她完全是对的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think she is.
sentences.zh: 对，我想是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, to be honest, I thought he was a bad man, but now that I've heard him speak.
sentences.zh: 我是说，说实话，我以前以为他是个坏人，但现在听过他讲话之后。

sentences.en: That's exactly how he spoke.
sentences.zh: 他说话就是这个调子。

sentences.en: I think he's even worse than I had imagined.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他比我想象的还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Not quite as bad as Himmler still, but maybe nudging up there.
sentences.zh: 虽然还比不上希姆莱，但也差不多快赶上了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's in the medals.
sentences.zh: 对，他简直能在奖牌榜上有名了。

sentences.en: He's on the podium, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他都站上领奖台了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Anyway, so Mary, understandably, she goes back to Edinburgh, to Holyrood and to her baby, little James, who is described by the English ambassador
sentences.zh: 言归正传，所以玛丽理所当然地回到了爱丁堡，回到了荷里路德宫，回到了她的小宝宝詹姆斯身边，英国大使曾这样描述过他

sentences.en: as being well proportioned and like to prove a godly prince.
sentences.zh: 身材匀称，将来很有希望成为一位虔诚的君主。

sentences.en: I mean, hasn't looked at his tongue, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，他当时肯定没检查这孩子的舌头。

sentences.en: And Mary is so anxious about what Darnley might get up to that she moves him from Holyrood to
sentences.zh: 玛丽对达利可能会搞出什么花样感到非常焦虑，于是她把达利从荷里路德宫转移到了

sentences.en: Stirling.
sentences.zh: 斯特林。

sentences.en: And en route, James is guarded by 500 musketeers.
sentences.zh: 在途中，有五百名火枪手负责护卫小詹姆斯。

sentences.en: And of course, Stirling is the very castle where Mary's mother, Mary of Guise, had taken her to keep her for safekeeping.
sentences.zh: 当然，斯特林正是当年玛丽的母亲吉斯的玛丽带她去避难的那座城堡。

sentences.en: And what Mary is worried about, I think, is that Darnley might seize James and appoint himself as regent.
sentences.zh: 我想，玛丽真正担心的是达利可能会劫持詹姆斯并自立为摄政王。

sentences.en: And that would then enable him essentially, perhaps even to imprison Mary, certainly to kind of sideline her and effectively rule Scotland as regent until James comes of age.
sentences.zh: 那将使他基本上能够甚至把玛丽软禁起来，当然也能把她边缘化，并在詹姆斯成年之前实际以摄政王的身份统治苏格兰。

sentences.en: So if Mary has control of James, then essentially she's blocking that option off for Darnley.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要玛丽掌控着詹姆斯，基本上就把达利的这条路给堵死了。

sentences.en: Mary recognises that the issue is what it's always been, which is that Darnley is not content with his status as a kind of a consort, that he wants to be king.
sentences.zh: 玛丽意识到，问题一直都在于达利并不满足于自己作为王夫的地位，他想当国王。

sentences.en: He wants to be the king of Scotland, which Mary had promised him and then had kind of changed her mind.
sentences.zh: 他想成为苏格兰的国王，而玛丽曾经答应过他，后来却又反悔了。

sentences.en: And because of this, Darnley is endlessly plotting.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，达利一直在无休止地密谋。

sentences.en: He's endlessly coming up with schemes.
sentences.zh: 他总是在想方设法搞阴谋。

sentences.en: So he's not just plotting to make himself king of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 所以他不仅在密谋让自己成为苏格兰国王。

sentences.en: Madly, he also wants to make himself king of England.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的是，他还想让自己成为英格兰国王。

sentences.en: He's come up with, I mean, just such a mad scheme.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他想出了一个如此疯狂的计划。

sentences.en: He wants to capture Scarborough.
sentences.zh: 他想要攻占斯卡伯勒。

sentences.en: Like Harold Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 就像哈拉尔·哈德拉达那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Scarborough is a rather, I mean, it's very picturesque, very attractive.
sentences.zh: 所以斯卡伯勒其实是个风景非常优美、迷人的地方。

sentences.en: It has a wonderful cricket festival, but it's not one of the great strongholds of England, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 那里有很棒的板球节，但我觉得客观来讲，它算不上英格兰的军事重镇。

sentences.en: It's a kind of fishing village on the Yorkshire coaSt. And the other stronghold he wants to get is the Scilly Isles, which are an archipelago off the southwest corner of Cornwall.
sentences.zh: 它只是约克郡海岸边的一个渔村。他想拿下的另一个据点是锡利群岛，那是康沃尔郡西南角外的一组群岛。

sentences.en: And his plan is that he's going to capture these places and then he's going to import Catholic armies from Europe.
sentences.zh: 他的计划是攻占这些地方，然后从欧洲引进天主教军队。

sentences.en: And he will then launch an invasion of England with these armies from Scarborough and the Scilly Isles.
sentences.zh: 接着他将率领这支从斯卡伯勒和锡利群岛出发的军队对英格兰发起入侵。

sentences.en: And it's completely mad.
sentences.zh: 这简直荒谬透顶。

sentences.en: We should actually remind listeners that Darnley is Catholic.
sentences.zh: 我们其实应该提醒听众，达利信仰天主教。

sentences.en: So this is part of the mix as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是整个事件的背景之一。

sentences.en: So this plot falls through, you know, it's absolutely stillborn.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个阴谋彻底泡汤了，可以说还没出生就夭折了。

sentences.en: He's humiliated by this.
sentences.zh: 他为此感到备受羞辱。

sentences.en: And so he then has a massive strop and announces that he is going to leave Mary.
sentences.zh: 于是他大发雷霆，宣称他要离开玛丽。

sentences.en: He's had enough of her and he's going to go and settle abroad.
sentences.zh: 他受够了玛丽，打算去国外定居。

sentences.en: And people might think, well, that's quite a good solution, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 人们可能会觉得，这倒是个挺不错的解决办法，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, it isn't.
sentences.zh: 其实不然。

sentences.en: Firstly, because it would be very humiliating for Mary and by extension Scotland.
sentences.zh: 首先，这会极大地羞辱玛丽，进而羞辱整个苏格兰。

sentences.en: But also it would be a nightmare for the Protestant lords because the last thing that they want is a Catholic with a claim to the throne
sentences.zh: 而且对新教贵族来说这也是一场噩梦，因为他们最不希望看到的就是一个对苏格兰王位

sentences.en: of Scotland, making mischief for them with the Catholic powers of France and Spain or whatever on the continent.
sentences.zh: 有继承权的天主教徒，在欧洲大陆勾结法兰西和西班牙等天主教势力来给他们制造麻烦。

sentences.en: And so they are irate about it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对此愤怒不已。

sentences.en: Mary is appalled.
sentences.zh: 玛丽震惊万分。

sentences.en: She spends a whole night trying to make him see sense, saying, you know, this is mad.
sentences.zh: 她花了一整夜试图让他恢复理智，说这太荒谬了，

sentences.en: Please don't do this.
sentences.zh: 请不要这么做。

sentences.en: He refuses.
sentences.zh: 但他拒绝了。

sentences.en: And so she summons the Privy Council and she orders Darnley to appear before the Privy Council.
sentences.zh: 于是她召集了枢密院，并命令达利在枢密院前出庭答话。

sentences.en: And the Privy Council asks Darnley to explain, you know, what are you up to?
sentences.zh: 枢密院质问达利到底想干什么，

sentences.en: What are you doing here?
sentences.zh: 你在这里究竟在搞什么名堂？

sentences.en: He can't really give a credible answer because basically his answer is, oh, you know, I'm cross.
sentences.zh: 他根本给不出一个可信的回答，因为说到底他的理由就是，哦，我很生气，

sentences.en: You know, you're not treating me right.
sentences.zh: 你们对我不好之类的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm going off on a gap yard.
sentences.zh: 没错，我要去过间隔年了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's basically his pitch.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上就是他的说辞。

sentences.en: And the Privy
sentences.zh: 枢密院

sentences.en: Council are so kind of stunned and appalled by what they've heard from him.
sentences.zh: 对从他嘴里听到的话感到震惊和骇异。

sentences.en: They write officially to
sentences.zh: 他们正式写信给

sentences.en: Catherine de' Medici in France and say, look, this guy is a lunatic, have nothing to do with him.
sentences.zh: 法国的凯瑟琳·德·美第奇，说道，听着，这家伙是个疯子，千万别跟他有任何瓜葛。

sentences.en: And if he does come to France and tries to set up, you know, a royal court in exile or to create mischief or whatever, you know, just do not touch him.
sentences.zh: 如果他真的来到法国，试图建立什么流亡朝廷或者制造麻烦之类的，千万不要搭理他。

sentences.en: And this, I think, is where the notion that he is a lunatic starts to come because Elizabeth in that letter that you quoted refers to him as being mad.
sentences.zh: 我想，认为他是疯子的说法就是从这里开始流传的，因为你刚才引用的那封信里伊丽莎白也说他疯了。

sentences.en: And I think that this is becoming part of the diplomatic chatter.
sentences.zh: 我想这已经成了外交闲聊的一部分。

sentences.en: He's such an international embarrassment that saying that he's mad is less of a humiliation than saying, well, we just can't control him.
sentences.zh: 他简直是个国际笑柄，与其承认“我们实在管不了他”，倒不如说他疯了受到的羞辱还少一些。

sentences.en: So with Darnley moving towards the sort of margins, does that mean that Mary now has to rely on a lot of people that she's previously fallen out with?
sentences.zh: 既然达利逐渐被边缘化，这是否意味着玛丽现在不得不重新依靠那些她以前曾与之交恶的人？

sentences.en: So, for example, if she's talking to the French, her foreign policy expert is this bloke, Maitland, who was her secretary of state, who had been disgraced after the Rizzio murder.
sentences.zh: 比如，当她与法国交涉时，她的外交政策专家就是梅特兰这家伙，他是她的国务秘书，在里齐奥谋杀案后曾一度失势。

sentences.en: Yeah, he had.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实失势过。

sentences.en: But I think he'd always basically been team Mary.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他基本上一直都是效忠玛丽阵营的。

sentences.en: And I think Mary knows that.
sentences.zh: 我想玛丽心里也清楚这一点。

sentences.en: And as you say, I mean, she needs his advice.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，她需要他的建言。

sentences.en: So he's brought out of his disgrace.
sentences.zh: 所以他被免除了罪名。

sentences.en: He's effectively pardoned and he's restored to his post as secretary of state.
sentences.zh: 他实际上得到了赦免，并恢复了国务秘书的职务。

sentences.en: But there is one condition.
sentences.zh: 但有一个条件。

sentences.en: And that is that Maitland is reconciled with the one Scottish lord on whom Mary is now relying more than any other because he has proved himself consistently loyal.
sentences.zh: 那就是梅特兰必须与那个苏格兰领主和解——玛丽现在比以往任何时候都更依赖他，因为他证明了自己始终如一的忠诚。

sentences.en: And this is the Earl of Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是博斯韦尔伯爵。

sentences.en: And Bothwell is this
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔这家伙

sentences.en: swaggering, muscle bound, got a tremendous ginger moustache.
sentences.zh: 盛气凌人、肌肉发达，还留着一撮极其显眼的红胡子。

sentences.en: Very fond of a punch up, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 客观来讲，他非常喜欢动手打架。

sentences.en: But he's been at Mary's back for a decade and more because he's stood behind Mary of Guise, her mother, when she'd been in trouble.
sentences.zh: 但他十多年来一直坚定地站在玛丽身后，因为当玛丽的母亲吉斯的玛丽陷入困境时，他曾挺身而出支持过她。

sentences.en: Bothwell had rallied to her cause in the wake of Rizzio's murder and Bothwell had helped to drive Morton and his fellow conspirators into exile.
sentences.zh: 在里齐奥遇害后，博斯韦尔迅速集结力量支持玛丽，并协助将莫顿及其同谋驱逐出境。

sentences.en: Bothwell, though, a very formidable man, is on the receiving end, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 不过，这个极其强悍的男人在那年秋天却遭到了袭击，不是吗？

sentences.en: That autumn.
sentences.zh: 那是当年秋天。

sentences.en: I mean, the most Scottish thing that's ever happened.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是史上最具有苏格兰特色的一幕了。

sentences.en: He's been attacked, left with life-threatening injuries by a man who's called...
sentences.zh: 他遇袭了，受了濒死的重伤，凶手是一个名叫……

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 快说啊。

sentences.en: What's he called, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 他叫什么名字，多米尼克？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's called Little Jock Elliot.
sentences.zh: 他叫小乔克·埃利奥特。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Surely he played for Dunferlin in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 他肯定在20世纪80年代为邓弗姆林队踢过球。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, Little Jock Elliot is a notorious reaver.
sentences.zh: 所以，小乔克·埃利奥特是个臭名昭著的强盗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Of course he is.
sentences.zh: 他当然是。

sentences.en: The reavers are the bandits who infest the border regions between England and Scotland, and particularly this region called the Debatable Lands, which is a stretch of the border.
sentences.zh: 那些强盗是盘踞在英格兰和苏格兰边境地区的匪徒，尤其是被称为“争议地带”的那片边境狭长地带。

sentences.en: And the hermitage, which is Bothwell's ancestral pile, is absolutely at the centre of the Debatable
sentences.zh: 而作为博斯韦尔家族祖宅的埃米塔奇城堡，正处在“争议地带”的

sentences.en: Lands.
sentences.zh: 核心区域。

sentences.en: I love the fact that after 700 episodes and people have been like, when are you going to do Scottish history?
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢这样一种情况：在做了700期节目后，大家总在问“你们什么时候才讲讲苏格兰历史？”

sentences.en: Do some Scottish history.
sentences.zh: 讲点苏格兰历史吧。

sentences.en: We could have done the Scottish Enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 我们本来可以讲苏格兰启蒙运动的。

sentences.en: We could have chosen any element, but instead we chose people head-butting each other in
sentences.zh: 我们本可以挑选任何题材，但我们偏偏选择了在争议地带互殴、名字叫小乔克的人，因为我们真的很想契合大众对苏格兰的固有印象。

sentences.en: Debatable Lands called Little Jock, because we absolutely wanted to lean into their sense of what Scotland is.
sentences.zh: 为了让苏格兰听众放心，争议地带不仅是苏格兰，也是全英国最无法无天、匪患猖獗的角落。

sentences.en: I mean, just to reassure Scottish listeners, the Debatable Lands are the most lawless and bandit-ridden corner, not just in Scotland, but in all of Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正在强调这一点。

sentences.en: So, we are emphasising that.
sentences.zh: 这显然也就是为什么博斯韦尔如此崇尚暴力，因为在这种环境下，你必须足够暴力才能立足。

sentences.en: And this clearly is why Bothwell is so given to violence, is that you have to be violent to hold your own in this kind of landscape.
sentences.zh: 所以，他遇袭了，浑身是伤，差点送命。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so he's attacked and left for dead, covered with all kinds of wounds.
sentences.zh: 消息传到了当时正在杰德堡的玛丽耳中，杰德堡在东面大约25英里外。当时她正在巡回审判。

sentences.en: The news is brought to Mary, who at the time is in Jedburgh, which is about 25 miles away to the eaSt. And she's on assizes.
sentences.zh: 所以，她四处奔走听取臣民的申诉，基本上是在履行她的皇室职责。

sentences.en: So, she's going around hearing complaints from her subjects, basically kind of showing herself doing her royal duties.
sentences.zh: 据后来流传的八卦称，玛丽一听到博斯韦尔遇袭的消息，就立刻离开杰德堡，独自骑马狂奔去了埃米塔奇城堡。

sentences.en: The gossip will be, that is reported later, is that the moment she hears the news that Bothwell has been attacked, she leaves Jedburgh and gallops off alone to the hermitage.
sentences.zh: 这不是真的。

sentences.en: This is not true.
sentences.zh: 她等了一个星期，因为她还要完成巡回审判，而且她也不是独自一人骑马前往的。

sentences.en: She waits for a week because she still has the assizes to hear and nor does she ride there alone.
sentences.zh: 她的同父异母兄弟莫里和她同行。

sentences.en: So, Morrie, her half-brother, he goes with her.
sentences.zh: 梅特兰也在场，还有庞大的随行队伍。

sentences.en: Maitland is there, a large retinue.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，这也算是一次惊人的骑马壮举，因为单程就有25英里，地形极其崎岖。

sentences.en: But even so, I mean, it is a startling feat of horsemanship because it's 25 miles there over really very rough terrain.
sentences.zh: 我去过那里亲眼看过，我非常敬佩

sentences.en: I mean, I've been there and seen it and I respect
sentences.zh: 玛丽能骑马走那么远的路。

sentences.en: Mary very highly for having travelled that far.
sentences.zh: 她在博斯韦尔的床边呆了两个小时，情况逐渐明朗：博斯韦尔不会死，他正在康复的路上。

sentences.en: She spends two hours by Bothwell's bedside and it becomes clear that Bothwell isn't going to die, that he's on the road to recovery.
sentences.zh: 然后他们又骑马赶了回来。

sentences.en: And then they ride back.
sentences.zh: 所以，那是非常充实且奔波的一天，对玛丽来说显然有些吃不消了。

sentences.en: So, that is a full and active day and it turns out to be too much for Mary.
sentences.zh: 她回到杰德堡后，便病倒了，而且病情非常危急。

sentences.en: She gets back to Jedburgh and she falls very, very dangerously ill.
sentences.zh: 无论是因为过度劳累，还是如果她曾经怀孕的话——她之前向达利提及过此事，不过此时她已经流产了。

sentences.en: So, whether it's overexertion, if she had been pregnant, she mentioned this to Darnley, I think by this point she's lost the baby.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能是流产后的并发症。

sentences.en: So, it may be the aftereffects of a miscarriage.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，人们都很担心她的生命安全。

sentences.en: But certainly, her life is feared for.
sentences.zh: 有一刻，她躺在床上足足半小时，“双眼紧闭，嘴唇紧闭，手脚僵硬冰冷”。

sentences.en: At one point, she lies in bed for half an hour and I quote, eyes closed, mouth fast and feet and arms stiff and cold.
sentences.zh: 她的同父异母兄弟莫里伯爵——我认为他内心充满了怨恨，嫉妒她是女王而自己不是国王，仅仅因为他是私生子而无法继承王位——

sentences.en: The Earl of Moray, her half-brother, who I think is consumed with resentment that she is the queen and he's not the king, you know, an accident of his illegitimacy.
sentences.zh: 开始动手搜刮她所有的银质餐具和戒指。

sentences.en: He starts laying hands on all her silver plate and rings.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像亨利五世在父亲咽气前就急着把王冠拿走一样。

sentences.en: So, it's like Henry V making off with the crown before his father is dead.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽并没有死，因为她有一位医术高超的法国医生，成功把她从鬼门关拉了回来。

sentences.en: And Mary doesn't die because she has a very skilful French doctor and he is able to kind of bring her back from the brink of death.
sentences.zh: 在看似快要不行的两周后，她就已经准备好继续行程了。

sentences.en: And two weeks on from when it seemed like she was going to die, she's ready to continue on her way.
sentences.zh: 这次濒死体验产生了极其深远的影响。

sentences.en: And the impact of this near-death experience is very profound.
sentences.zh: 对玛丽而言，我想她真的开始思考：我究竟会留下一个什么样的王国？

sentences.en: I think for Mary, I think that she really starts to think, you know, what kind of kingdom am I going to leave behind?
sentences.zh: 这在苏格兰贵族中引发了巨大的焦虑高潮。

sentences.en: It generates a massive anxiety spike among the Scottish nobility.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望政权发生更迭。

sentences.en: They don't want a change of regime.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望达利在外胡作非为。

sentences.en: They don't want Darnley on the loose.
sentences.zh: 他们担心这会导致无政府状态。

sentences.en: They are worried that it will result in anarchy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们坚决支持让玛丽继续坐在王位上，并确保达利不会给她带来太多麻烦。

sentences.en: And so, they are very committed to keeping Mary on the throne and ensuring that Darnley doesn't cause her too much trouble.
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，我们该如何处置达利？

sentences.en: And the question then is, well, how are we going to deal with Darnley?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们该如何确保玛丽不会再被他无休止的麻烦给缠身？

sentences.en: I mean, how are we going to make sure that Mary isn't kind of embroiled in endless trouble from him?
sentences.zh: 他们到底能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: What on earth could they possibly do?
sentences.zh: 我们还能做什么？

sentences.en: What could we do?
sentences.zh: 正是国务秘书梅特兰——当初曾用非常微妙、含沙射影的言辞首次提议谋杀里齐奥的那个人——现在再次开始试探

sentences.en: And it is Maitland, the Secretary of State, who was the guy who had first suggested the murder of Rizzio in very kind of subtle, insinuating terms, who again now starts to broach
sentences.zh: 也许可以策划另一场谋杀的可能性。

sentences.en: the possibility, maybe, of another murder.
sentences.zh: 所以他甚至不惜将这个想法诉诸文字。

sentences.en: So, he even goes so far as to kind of put this into writing.
sentences.zh: 所以他甚至不惜将这个想法诉诸文字。

sentences.en: So, he writes to the Scottish ambassador in Paris shortly after Mary has had this brush with death.
sentences.zh: 因此，在玛丽经历这场生死劫难后不久，他就给巴黎的苏格兰大使写了信。

sentences.en: It is a heartbreak for her to think that he should be her husband and how to be free of him.
sentences.zh: 想到他竟然是自己的丈夫，以及该如何摆脱他，对她来说简直心碎。

sentences.en: She sees no way out.
sentences.zh: 她看不到任何出路。

sentences.en: But obviously, you know, he is suggesting that he might.
sentences.zh: 但显然，你知道的，他在暗示自己或许有办法。

sentences.en: He is travelling with Mary from Jedburgh and they go to a place called Craig Miller Castle and they arrive there on the 20th of November.
sentences.zh: 他和玛丽从杰德堡出发，前往一个叫克雷格米勒城堡的地方，并在11月20日抵达那里。

sentences.en: It's just south of Edinburgh and it's Laird is Catholic, which means that he is absolutely reliable.
sentences.zh: 它就在爱丁堡南部，其庄园主是天主教徒，这意味着他绝对可靠。

sentences.en: I mean, he's completely team Mary.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他完全是玛丽这一边的。

sentences.en: And Mary gets there and she then falls ill again.
sentences.zh: 玛丽到达那里后，随后又病倒了。

sentences.en: And so, all the lords in her retinue, which include Maitland, Moray, and by this time, Bothwell, because he's risen up from his sickbed.
sentences.zh: 因此，她随从中的所有领主——包括梅特兰、莫雷，以及此时已经病愈起身的博思韦尔——

sentences.en: He's covered in scars, but he's, you know, he's kind of rough and tough.
sentences.zh: 他身上满是伤疤，但你知道的，他那种人有点粗犷硬朗。

sentences.en: They all have time while she's lying in her sickbed to discuss what might be done with Darnley.
sentences.zh: 趁着她卧病在床，他们都有时间讨论该如何处置达利。

sentences.en: And when Mary recovers, they go to see her, all except for Moray, who by this
sentences.zh: 等玛丽康复后，他们前去拜访她，除了莫雷之外所有人悉数到场，而莫雷此时

sentences.en: point is worried at the way in which the conversation is turning and doesn't really want to be a part of it.
sentences.zh: 对谈话的发展方向感到担忧，其实并不想参与其中。

sentences.en: But Maitland and Bothwell and all the other lads, they go to Mary and they say, look, you have got to divorce Darnley.
sentences.zh: 但梅特兰、博思韦尔和其他小伙子们去找玛丽说，听着，你必须和达利离婚。

sentences.en: Moray does not think that she should divorce Darnley because that would just leave him on the loose.
sentences.zh: 莫雷认为她不应该和达利离婚，因为那会让他逍遥法外。

sentences.en: But all the others think, yeah, let's go for it.
sentences.zh: 但其他人则认为，行吧，就这么办。

sentences.en: Mary listens to them and she kind of agrees in principle, but her anxiety obviously is that it wouldn't be damaging to
sentences.zh: 玛丽听取了他们的意见，原则上也算同意了，但她显然担心这会不会对

sentences.en: James.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯造成损害。

sentences.en: She says, I will have it provided it is not prejudicial to my son.
sentences.zh: 她说，我可以答应，前提是对我儿子没有损害。

sentences.en: And then she asks, well, is Moray, does he agree to this?
sentences.zh: 然后她问，那么，莫雷，他同意这件事吗？

sentences.en: Because I noticed he's not here.
sentences.zh: 因为我注意到他不在场。

sentences.en: And Maitland answers, I am assured he will look through his fingers thereto and will behold our doings saying nothing to the same.
sentences.zh: 梅特兰回答说，我确信他会对此睁一只眼闭一只眼，看着我们行事而对此一言不发。

sentences.en: In other words, he's just going to let us kind of get on with it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他只是打算让我们继续做下去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And obviously if it was just a divorce, it wouldn't be such a big deal.
sentences.zh: 显然，如果这只是一场离婚，倒也没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: But that implies that this may be more than a divorce, that it may be a slightly more permanent separation, shall we say.
sentences.zh: 但这暗示着，这可能不仅仅是一场离婚，我们可以说，这可能是一场稍微更永久的分离。

sentences.en: That is a hint that Maitland then drops to Mary, which Mary becomes very agitated.
sentences.zh: 那是梅特兰随后向玛丽暗示的一点，这让玛丽变得非常激动。

sentences.en: And she presses
sentences.zh: 她追问

sentences.en: Maitland, well, you know, what exactly do you mean?
sentences.zh: 梅特兰，你知道的，你到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: And she goes on to say, I will that ye do nothing whereto any spot may be laid to my honour or conscience.
sentences.zh: 她接着说道，我希望你们不要做任何会给我的名誉或良心留下污点的事。

sentences.en: And therefore I pray you rather let the matter be in the state as it is, i.e. don't murder him.
sentences.zh: 因此我请求你们，还是让事情保持原状吧，也就是说：别谋杀他。

sentences.en: And for now, let's leave the whole question of divorce to one side.
sentences.zh: 至于现在，让我们把离婚的问题暂且放在一边。

sentences.en: But the clock is ticking a little bit, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但时间在一点点流逝，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because they're going to christen James, their son.
sentences.zh: 因为他们要为儿子詹姆斯受洗。

sentences.en: And I suppose if Darnley had turned up to that and sort of asserted himself as James's father, that might have slightly changed the game.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果达利当时出现并以詹姆斯父亲的身份宣示主权，那可能会稍微改变局面。

sentences.en: But very foolishly, it happens at Stirling, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 但非常愚蠢的是，仪式是在斯特灵举行的，不是吗？

sentences.en: 17th of December.
Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Darnley has a massive tantrum and refuses to come because he's crossed that he's not king.
sentences.zh: 达利大发雷霆，拒绝出席，因为他气恼自己不是国王。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's such poor behaviour to miss the christening of your own son because, you know, you can't wear a crown.
sentences.zh: 因为你戴不上王冠，就错过自己儿子的受洗仪式，这行为实在太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he's not there.
sentences.zh: 所以他不在场。

sentences.en: There is a man on hand who Mary can turn to, to take down his place.
sentences.zh: 现场有一个人是玛丽可以求助来替代他位置的。

sentences.en: And this is the much scarred and mustachioed Earl of Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个满脸伤疤、留着八字胡的博思韦尔伯爵。

sentences.en: You know, he's got to look smart for the occasion.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他得在这个场合显得精干。

sentences.en: And so Mary makes sure to provide him with a very fine outfit of kind of gorgeous blue clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽特地为他提供了一套非常精美、华丽的蓝色服装。

sentences.en: And so Bothwell is strutting around looking tremendous.
sentences.zh: 于是博思韦尔昂首阔步地走着，显得威风凛凛。

sentences.en: And of course, this is much noted.
sentences.zh: 当然，这受到了极大的关注。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: People observe that Darnley isn't there, but Bothwell's looking great in his suit.
sentences.zh: 人们注意到达利不在，但博思韦尔穿着那套衣服看起来好极了。

sentences.en: But even
sentences.zh: 但甚至

sentences.en: Bothwell refuses to attend the christening.
sentences.zh: 连博思韦尔也拒绝出席受洗仪式。

sentences.en: And so does Moray, Bothwell's old rival, Mary's half sister, because they're Protestants.
sentences.zh: 莫雷也是如此——博思韦尔的老对手、玛丽的同母异父姐姐——因为他们是新教徒。

sentences.en: And the ceremony, the baptism, is a Catholic one.
sentences.zh: 而这个仪式，也就是洗礼，是一场天主教的仪式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it might look as though the whole thing has been a disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来可能就像整件事是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Darnley's not there.
sentences.zh: 达利不在。

sentences.en: Bothwell is, you know, creating gossip.
sentences.zh: 博思韦尔在，你知道的，这引发了闲话。

sentences.en: Bothwell and Moray aren't attending the baptism.
sentences.zh: 博思韦尔和莫雷都没有出席洗礼。

sentences.en: But actually, it's been a triumph behind the scenes, because what has been happening while the Lords have been
sentences.zh: 但实际上，幕后这可以说是一场胜利，因为在领主们一直在

sentences.en: plotting what to do about Darnley is that Mary, you know, I said that, you know, her mind has really been concentrated.
sentences.zh: 密谋如何处置达利的同时，玛丽，你知道的，我刚才说过，她的心思其实高度集中。

sentences.en: She's really thinking, well, what do I want from the future?
sentences.zh: 她真的在想，我到底对未来有什么期待？

sentences.en: And so she has written to Elizabeth in England, queen to queen, not going through Maitland, not going through Cecil.
sentences.zh: 于是她写信给英格兰的伊丽莎白，以女王对女王的身份，没有通过梅特兰，也没有通过塞西尔。

sentences.en: And she says to Elizabeth, look, I've very nearly died.
sentences.zh: 她对伊丽莎白说，听着，我差点死掉。

sentences.en: And I've been worrying about my son.
sentences.zh: 我一直很担心我的儿子。

sentences.en: So what I request is that if I die, would you become James's protector, which in effect means becoming James's foster mother.
sentences.zh: 所以我请求的是，如果我死了，你愿意成为詹姆斯的保护人吗？这实际上意味着成为詹姆斯的养母。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth is very touched by this.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白对此深受感动。

sentences.en: And she accepts.
sentences.zh: 并且她接受了。

sentences.en: And as a token of this, she agrees to be James's godmother, even though the baptism ceremony is a Catholic one.
sentences.zh: 作为象征，她同意成为詹姆斯的教母，尽管洗礼仪式是一场天主教仪式。

sentences.en: And she sends
sentences.zh: 她给

sentences.en: Mary this magnificent bejeweled font of solid gold.
sentences.zh: 玛丽送去了这座镶满珠宝、由纯金打造的宏伟洗礼盘。

sentences.en: And the detente between the two queens, you know, relations between them had been quite tense.
sentences.zh: 两位女王之间的缓和——你知道的，她们之间的关系过去相当紧张。

sentences.en: It's now sufficient that they can continue to discuss policy without recourse to their respective ministers and begin privately negotiating
sentences.zh: 现在已经好转到她们可以直接讨论政策，而无需通过各自的大臣，并开始私下谈判

sentences.en: over what had always been Mary's ultimate dream, namely to be acknowledged by Elizabeth as heir apparent to the throne of England.
sentences.zh: 关于玛丽一直以来的终极梦想，即被伊丽莎白承认为英格兰王位的法定继承人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's looking good for Mary.
sentences.zh: 这对玛丽来说是个好兆头。

sentences.en: It is looking good for Mary.
sentences.zh: 这对玛丽来说确实是个好兆头。

sentences.en: And it was her illness that precipitated this kind of diplomatic breakthrough, you know, that this private conversation.
sentences.zh: 正是她的病促成了这种外交突破，你知道的，也就是这场私下对话。

sentences.en: And I think also as part of this,
sentences.zh: 我想这也是其中的一部分，

sentences.en: Mary is thinking, I'm reconciled with Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 玛丽在想，我和伊丽莎白言归于好了。

sentences.en: Why don't I get everybody else to be reconciled?
sentences.zh: 为什么我不能让其他所有人都言归于好呢？

sentences.en: So on Christmas Eve, she formally pardons the Rizzio plotters.
sentences.zh: 于是在平安夜，她正式赦免了里奇奥阴谋的策划者。

sentences.en: So that's Morton and all that gang.
sentences.zh: 也就是莫顿和他的那一帮人。

sentences.en: On the 6th of January, she allows Maitland to marry Posh Mary, the one of the four Marys who Maitland had been desperately in love with despite the 20 year age gap.
sentences.zh: 1月6日，她允许梅特兰迎娶“俏玛丽”（四个玛丽之一，尽管年龄相差20岁，梅特兰对她爱得死去活来）。

sentences.en: And on the 9th of January, Morton crosses from Berwick into Scotland.
sentences.zh: 1月9日，莫顿从贝里克越境进入苏格兰。

sentences.en: He is home.
sentences.zh: 他回家了。

sentences.en: And on the 14th of January, Morton and Maitland meet at a place called Whittingham Castle, which is again, a few miles a ride from Edinburgh, all these castles
sentences.zh: 1月14日，莫顿和梅特兰在一个叫惠廷汉姆城堡的地方会面，这里同样距离爱丁堡只有几英里的骑行路程，这些城堡星罗棋布地散落在首都周围。

sentences.en: dotted around the capital.
sentences.zh: 资本。

sentences.en: And present for their meeting is their old adversary from the Rizzio plot, the man who Mary had turned to when Rizzio got murdered, the Earl of Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 出席他们会议的是他们在里奇奥阴谋中的老对手，也就是在里奇奥被谋杀时玛丽曾求助过的那个人——博思韦尔伯爵。

sentences.en: So amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 两拨不同的人聚在一起商讨事情。

sentences.en: I mean, what could they be discussing, these three men?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这三个人到底在讨论什么？

sentences.en: While all that's happening, what's happened to Darnley?
sentences.zh: 在这一切发生的同时，达利怎么了？

sentences.en: He refused to come to the baptism of his own son.

sentences.zh: 就在达恩利预定要返回荷里路德宫的前一天晚上，玛丽带着一大群领主和女士在傍晚时分抵达，

sentences.en: Bothwell very prominent among them.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔也在其中非常显眼。

sentences.en: And they're celebrating this.
sentences.zh: 他们在庆祝这件事。

sentences.en: They're celebrating the fact that Darnley will be coming back to join Mary the following day.
sentences.zh: 他们在庆祝达恩利第二天将回来与玛丽团聚的事实。

sentences.en: And Mary is in an excellent mood.
sentences.zh: 玛丽的心情非常好。

sentences.en: She feels that she's got Darnley back under her influence.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己把达恩利重新拉回了自己的掌控之中。

sentences.en: He seems much more amenable than he had been.
sentences.zh: 他看起来比以前好说话多了。

sentences.en: And that evening, Darnley is off his face on whiskey.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，达恩利喝威士忌喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: He's developed a real taste for it.
sentences.zh: 他已经真正培养出了对威士忌的爱好。

sentences.en: He starts groping her very publicly in front of everyone.
sentences.zh: 他开始当着所有人的面公然对她上下其手。

sentences.en: And rather than giving him a slap or telling him to leave her alone, she gives him a ring as a token of her affection.
sentences.zh: 她没有给他一巴掌或叫他别烦她，而是送了他一枚戒指作为她爱意的象征。

sentences.en: So things seem to be looking up for the happy couple.
sentences.zh: 所以这对幸福的夫妇看起来一切都在向好的方向发展。

sentences.en: But I think the real reason that she's happy has nothing to do with Darnley and everything to do with these ongoing private negotiations with Elizabeth in
sentences.zh: 但我认为她高兴的真正原因与达恩利无关，而完全与这些正在进行的和英国伊丽莎白的秘密谈判有关。

sentences.en: England.
sentences.zh: 英国。

sentences.en: It really looks now as though Mary's great dream of being publicly acknowledged as Elizabeth's heir might be on the verge of fulfilment.
sentences.zh: 现在看起来确实像是玛丽长期以来的伟大梦想——被公开承认为伊丽莎白的继承人——可能正处于实现的边缘。

sentences.en: I mean, very hard to know with Elizabeth because she's always kind of playing hard to get.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对伊丽莎白很难捉摸，因为她总是摆出高姿态。

sentences.en: But Mary, I think, genuinely believes that her great dream might be close to fulfilment.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽，我认为她真心相信她的伟大梦想可能接近实现了。

sentences.en: So Darnley wants Mary to stay with him the night, but Mary doesn't because one of her favourite servants has got married that afternoon and is holding a great
sentences.zh: 所以达恩利想让玛丽留下来陪他过夜，但玛丽没有留下，因为她最喜欢的仆人之一那天下午结婚了，正在举行一场盛大的

sentences.en: celebration, a kind of wedding mask.
sentences.zh: 庆典，一种婚礼假面舞会。

sentences.en: And Mary has promised to go.
sentences.zh: 玛丽答应了要去。

sentences.en: And Mary always keeps her promises to her servants.
sentences.zh: 而且玛丽总是信守对仆人们的承诺。

sentences.en: And of course, also, you know, she likes to dance.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道的，她也喜欢跳舞。

sentences.en: She doesn't want to miss out on that.
sentences.zh: 她不想错过这个。

sentences.en: So she leaves Darnley.
sentences.zh: 所以她离开了达恩利。

sentences.en: She arrives back at Holyrood about 11 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 她在11点左右回到了荷里路德宫。

sentences.en: She attends her servant's mask, but she doesn't stay too long.
sentences.zh: 她出席了仆人的假面舞会，但她没有呆太久。

sentences.en: She's in bed by half past midnight.
sentences.zh: 她在午夜十二点半前就上床睡觉了。

sentences.en: And then at two o'clock, so an hour and a half later, she is woken by the destruction of Darnley's house at Kirker Fields.
sentences.zh: 然后在两点钟，也就是一个半小时后，她被柯克费尔德达恩利住所的毁灭声惊醒。

sentences.en: And having heard the explosion, she summons Bothwell, who of course is the sheriff of Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 听到爆炸声后，她召来了博斯韦尔，他当然是爱丁堡的治安官。

sentences.en: So it's his responsibility to investigate and Bothwell goes off.
sentences.zh: 所以调查是他的责任，博斯韦尔便出发了。

sentences.en: And when he comes back and he says that the house has been blown up and that Darnley has been found dead, witnesses are pretty much agreed that she is appalled by the news.
sentences.zh: 当他回来并说房子被炸毁、达恩利被发现死亡时，目击者基本一致认为她对这个消息感到震惊。

sentences.en: And in a way that one might think is perhaps typical of Mary, she's appalled less for Darnley than by the thought that it might have been targeted at her.
sentences.zh: 以一种人们可能会认为或许是玛丽典型反应的方式，她感到震惊与其说是为了达恩利，不如说是担心这可能是针对她而来的。

sentences.en: She says, this crime was dressed as well for us as for the king, for we lay the most part of all the
sentences.zh: 她说，这个罪行不仅是针对国王，也是针对我们而策划的，因为我们在

sentences.en: last week in that same lodging and was there accompanied with the most part of the lords that are in this town that same night.
sentences.zh: 上周的大部分时间里都住在那个住处，那天晚上镇上的大部分领主也都陪伴在那里。

sentences.en: So it's all about her basically.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上这全是为了她自己。

sentences.en: But also, and I think the, you know, an extra reason why she's devastated is that she knows how Darnley's murder is going to land across Europe.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为她感到崩溃的另一个原因是，她知道达恩利被谋杀的消息在整个欧洲会引起怎样的反响。

sentences.en: You know, this is going to be seen by the crowned heads of Christendom as regicide, which they obviously view as being a terrible crime.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这会被基督教世界的君主们视为弑君罪，他们显然认为这是一桩滔天大罪。

sentences.en: They rank him as a king, even though he isn't one.
sentences.zh: 他们把他当作国王看待，尽管他其实不是。

sentences.en: He's married to a queen.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一位女王。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not officially a king, but they will see it as effectively being regicide.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他不是官方承认的国王，但他们会认为这实际上就是弑君。

sentences.en: And she knows that one person who will be absolutely appalled is her royal cousin,
sentences.zh: 她知道有一个人一定会感到无比震惊，那就是她的皇室表妹，

sentences.en: Elizabeth of England, with whom she has been in negotiations.
sentences.zh: 英格兰的伊丽莎白，她一直在与对方进行谈判。

sentences.en: So that I think is the key point.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这是关键点。

sentences.en: The timing of Darnley's murder for Mary could not have been worse.
sentences.zh: 对玛丽来说，达恩利被谋杀的时机再糟糕不过了。

sentences.en: So if Mary didn't authorise or approve the murder, then who did?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果玛丽没有授权或批准这场谋杀，那是谁干的？

sentences.en: Well, by early May, you remember we've got this Englishman in Berwick.
sentences.zh: 好了，到了五月初，还记得我们在伯威克的那个英国人吗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This guy, Sir William Drury, he thinks he has cracked the case.
sentences.zh: 这家伙，威廉·德鲁里爵士，他认为自己已经破案了。

sentences.en: And so he writes to Cecil, and he names the two leading culprits.
sentences.zh: 于是他写信给塞西尔，并点出了两个主要罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: And probably the name of these two leading culprits will not come as a surprise to listeners.
sentences.zh: 这两个主要罪魁祸首的名字对听众来说可能并不意外。

sentences.en: Morton, Drury writes, is noted to have assured friendship to Bothwell, which to be the thankful and now for his favour showed him in his absence and trouble.
sentences.zh: 德鲁里写道，据信莫頓曾向博斯韦尔承诺友谊，以此感谢并回报对方在他缺席和陷入困境时给予他的关照。

sentences.en: He intendeth to continue.
sentences.zh: 他打算将这种友谊继续下去。

sentences.en: And this is a brilliant piece of detective work.
sentences.zh: 这是一次极其精彩的侦探工作。

sentences.en: Most people think that
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为

sentences.en: Bothwell and Morton are deadly enemies.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔和莫頓是死敌。

sentences.en: They'd been on opposed sides in the imbroglio around the murder of Rizzio.
sentences.zh: 他们在围绕里奇奥谋杀案的纷争中曾处于对立的两派。

sentences.en: But actually, what Drury has found out is that it was Bothwell who had pushed Mary to pardon Morton.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，德鲁里发现的是，正是博斯韦尔敦促玛丽赦免莫頓。

sentences.en: And the reason that he had done that was because Bothwell knew that even though he'd been opposed to Morton over the Rizzio plot, any resentment that Morton might feel towards
sentences.zh: 他这么做的原因是因为博斯韦尔知道，尽管他在里奇奥阴谋中曾与莫頓对立，但莫頓对博斯韦尔可能怀有的任何怨恨，与莫頓对因里奇奥阴谋背叛过他的达恩利的刻骨仇恨相比，根本不值一提。

sentences.en: Bothwell is as nothing compared to the utter loathing that Morton has for Darnley, who had double-crossed him over the Rizzio plot.
sentences.zh: 所以博斯韦尔、莫頓还有梅特兰在1月14日会面并进行了讨论。

sentences.en: And so Bothwell and Morton and Maitland as well had met up on the 14th of January and they had had discussions.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一半节目中留下了悬念。

sentences.en: And we left it hanging in the previous half.
sentences.zh: 这些讨论是关于什么的？

sentences.en: What were these discussions about?
sentences.zh: 好吧，德鲁里已经查清了这些讨论的内容。

sentences.en: Well, Drury has found out what these discussions were about.
sentences.zh: 他们当时是在密谋暗杀达恩利。

sentences.en: They were committing themselves to the murder of Darnley.
sentences.zh: 他们当时是在承诺谋杀达恩利。

sentences.en: Very rapidly, they had succeeded in signing up large numbers of other prominent Scottish nobles.
sentences.zh: 他们非常迅速地成功拉拢了许多其他杰出的苏格兰贵族。

sentences.en: What had motivated all of them, so Morton is obviously motivated by personal resentment, but the number of people who were prepared
sentences.zh: 是什么激励了所有人，所以莫顿显然是出于个人的怨恨，但准备好

sentences.en: to sign up to the murder of Darnley reflects the fact that he is seen as a massive, massive problem to be eliminated.
sentences.zh: 参与谋杀达恩利的人数反映出一个事实，即他被视为一个必须被清除的巨大、巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And it's very telling, for instance, that one of the conspirators seems to have been the laird of Trackair, who was the man who had witnessed Darnley's terrible behaviour at his
sentences.zh: 而且很有说明意义的是，例如，其中一个阴谋者似乎是特拉克尔的庄园主，他曾亲眼目睹达恩利在

sentences.en: house.
sentences.zh: 府邸中的可怕行为。

sentences.en: Darnley's residents in Kirker Fields provide the conspirators with the perfect opportunity.
sentences.zh: 达恩利在柯克菲尔斯的住所为阴谋者提供了绝佳的机会。

sentences.en: But of course, the moment he leaves Kirker Field and goes back to Mary, it then becomes much harder to eliminate him without also killing Mary, which they don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 但当然，一旦他离开柯克菲尔斯回到玛丽身边，那么要在不杀死玛丽的情况下清除他就变得困难得多，而这并非他们所愿。

sentences.en: And Bothwell, who has been in close attendance on Mary throughout, I mean, he's absolutely keeping abreast of Darnley's potential movements.
sentences.zh: 而博思韦尔一直密切陪同在玛丽身边，我的意思是，他绝对紧跟达恩利潜在的动向。

sentences.en: And so that's why it's the night before he's due to leave that they realise, well, we've got to go for it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么就在他预定离开的前一天晚上，他们意识到，好吧，我们必须动手了。

sentences.en: It is also Bothwell who supplies the gunpowder for the explosion, and he can do that because he is the sheriff of Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 也是博思韦尔为爆炸提供了火药，他能做到这一点是因为他是爱丁堡的治安官。

sentences.en: And so people would expect to see him in charge of men who were kind of, you know, rumbling through the streets of Edinburgh with wagons or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因此人们会期望看到他指挥着那些在爱丁堡街头推着马车之类东西的人。

sentences.en: So on the evening of the 9th of February, as Mary and Darnley are partying in the rooms above them, Morton's men are mining the cellars of the house.
sentences.zh: 所以在2月9日傍晚，当玛丽和达恩利在他们楼上的房间里聚会时，莫顿的手下正在挖掘房子的地窖。

sentences.en: And in fact, Mary runs into one of these people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，玛丽碰巧遇到了其中一个人。

sentences.en: He'd been a page of Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 他曾是博思韦尔的侍童。

sentences.en: He's now become a valet to Mary, and he has the nickname of French Paris.
sentences.zh: 他现在成了玛丽的贴身男仆，人称“法国巴黎”。

sentences.en: And Mary sees him and says, Jesus, Paris, how begrimed you are.
sentences.zh: 玛丽看到他便说：“天哪，巴黎，你身上怎么这么脏。”

sentences.en: What a thing to say to somebody.
sentences.zh: 对人说这种话。

sentences.en: I mean, mad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，太疯狂了。

sentences.en: His face is streaked, but Mary can see through the dirt that he is blushing.
sentences.zh: 他的脸上有道道污痕，但玛丽能透过污垢看到他在脸红。

sentences.en: But he says nothing, just twists his cap.
sentences.zh: 但他什么也没说，只是扭着帽子。

sentences.en: How begrimed you are.
sentences.zh: “你身上怎么这么脏。”

sentences.en: I'd like to use that.
sentences.zh: 我想用这句话。

sentences.en: I'm going to use that line.
sentences.zh: 我要用这句台词。

sentences.en: You can use it to Arthur, surely, if he's...
sentences.zh: 你当然可以用它来对付亚瑟，如果他……

sentences.en: I will.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: Well, he's always begrimed, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 好吧，说实话，他总是脏兮兮的。

sentences.en: What I don't understand, right, I get the explosion.
sentences.zh: 我不明白的是，对吧，我懂爆炸的事。

sentences.en: Begrimed people have mined this building, and it's blown up.
sentences.zh: 满脸污垢的人挖了这座建筑，然后它爆炸了。

sentences.en: What I don't get is why Darnley didn't die in the explosion.
sentences.zh: 我不明白的是为什么达恩利没有在爆炸中死掉。

sentences.en: Why is he lying in the garden next to a chair, a rope, and a cloak?
sentences.zh: 为什么他会躺在花园里的一把椅子、一根绳子和一件斗篷旁边？

sentences.en: Are the Freemasons involved in some peculiar way before being founded?
sentences.zh: 难道共济会在它成立之前就以某种奇特的方式参与其中了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is the whole Agatha Christie dimension to it, which has always so intrigued and fascinated people, and I think complicated attempts to solve the murder.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是其中带有阿加莎·克里斯蒂风格的维度，它总是让人着迷和好奇，而且我认为这让试图破译这起谋杀案变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: Guy's explanation, which is essentially a refinement of the reports that Drury has been sending to Cecil.
sentences.zh: 盖伊的解释，本质上是对德鲁里发给塞西尔的报告的提炼。

sentences.en: So I think Drury is the guy who really nails it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为德鲁里才是真正搞清楚真相的人。

sentences.en: Drury reports to Cecil that on the night of Darnley's murder, he suspects nothing of what is to come.
sentences.zh: 德鲁里向塞西尔报告说，在达恩利被谋杀的那天晚上，他对外面的风吹草动毫无察觉。

sentences.en: He makes his farewells to Mary, and then he goes to bed.
sentences.zh: 他向玛丽告别，然后上床睡觉。

sentences.en: And shortly afterwards, he's woken by the sounds of muffled footsteps from below.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，他被楼下传来的沉闷脚步声吵醒。

sentences.en: He looks out of a side window, and he sees kind of shadowy cloaked figures stealthily moving around.
sentences.zh: 他向侧窗外望去，看到一些披着斗篷的可疑身影在鬼鬼祟祟地四处走动。

sentences.en: And he is a guy who knows he has lots of enemies.
sentences.zh: 他是一个深知自己有很多敌人的人。

sentences.en: And so he assumes the worst, and he reaches for a thick fur cloak.
sentences.zh: 所以他做最坏的打算，伸手去抓一件厚重的毛皮斗篷。

sentences.en: He then wakes his valet and other servants, and he goes to a window that looks directly out over the city wall, which kind of adjoins the house in which he's in.
sentences.zh: 然后他叫醒了他的男仆和其他仆人，走到一扇正对城市城墙的窗户前，那堵墙与他所在的房子相邻。

sentences.en: The servants get a chair, and they tie a rope to this chair, and they then lower Darnley and his valet into the street below, so outside the city wall.
sentences.zh: 仆人们搬来一把椅子，将一根绳子系在椅子上，然后把达恩利和他的男仆放到了下面的街道上，也就是城墙外面。

sentences.en: However, disaster.
sentences.zh: 然而，灾难发生了。

sentences.en: Drury's greatest investigative achievement has been to identify what happens next, and in particular, to identify the
sentences.zh: 德鲁里最伟大的调查成就，是查明了接下来发生的事情，特别是认出了

sentences.en: man who had been on patrol in the street in case of just such an eventuality.
sentences.zh: 那个为了防范此类突发事件而一直在街头巡逻的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is a guy we've already met.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们已经见过的那个人。

sentences.en: He's a bloke called Andrew Kerr of Faldenside, and he was the man who, in the course of the Rizzio murder, had pointed a loaded gun at Mary's pregnant belly.
sentences.zh: 这家伙叫法尔登赛的安德鲁·克尔，他正是在里齐奥谋杀案中，曾用上膛的枪指着玛丽怀孕肚子的那个人。

sentences.en: He, as one of the Rizzio conspirators, is as consumed with hatred for Darnley as Morton.
sentences.zh: 作为里齐奥的阴谋者之一，他对达恩利有着和莫顿一样深切的仇恨。

sentences.en: And like Morton, is absolutely set on getting his revenge.
sentences.zh: 而且和莫顿一样，他绝对一心想要报仇。

sentences.en: And this is despite the fact that Darnley is actually a kinsman of Andrew Kerr.
sentences.zh: 尽管事实上达恩利其实是安德鲁·克尔的亲戚。

sentences.en: And to this end, Kerr, like Morton, has teamed up with Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 为此，克尔和莫顿一样，与博思韦尔联手了。

sentences.en: And Drury writes to Cecil and details what happened next.
sentences.zh: 德鲁里给塞西尔写信，详细描述了接下来发生的事情。

sentences.en: The king was long of dying, and to his strengths made debate for his life, which essentially means that he had tried to reason with Kerr and his men.
sentences.zh: “国王临死前挣扎了很久，为了保命而据理力争，”这基本上意味着他曾试图与克尔及其手下讲道理。

sentences.en: And this report is substantiated in a remarkable way by the testimony of old women who lived in cottages on the side of this road, and who were interrogated by agents of
sentences.zh: 这份报告得到了惊人的证实，其依据是居住在这条路旁小屋里的老妇人们的证词，她们受到了

sentences.en: the Scottish Privy Council.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰枢密院特工的审问。

sentences.en: And one of these women reported hearing Darnley cry out,
sentences.zh: 其中一位妇人报告说听到达恩利大声呼喊：

sentences.en: Oh, my kinsman, have mercy on me for the love of him who had mercy on all the world.
sentences.zh: “哦，我的亲人，看在那位怜悯全世之人的份上，对我施以怜悯吧。”

sentences.en: But it's no good.
sentences.zh: 但无济于事。

sentences.en: Darnley and his valet are both strangled.
sentences.zh: 达恩利和他的男仆都被勒死了。

sentences.en: So that's why there are no marks on their bodies.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们的尸体上没有任何痕迹。

sentences.en: And then they are taken and laid out in a neighbouring garden.
sentences.zh: 然后他们被带到附近的花园里摆放好。

sentences.en: And the chair, the rope, and the cloak are dumped beside them.
sentences.zh: 椅子、绳子和斗篷都被扔在他们旁边。

sentences.en: Now, the issue obviously is Darnley is dead.
sentences.zh: 现在，问题显然是达恩利已经死了。

sentences.en: So do they need to blow up the house?
sentences.zh: 那他们还有必要炸毁房子吗？

sentences.en: The problem is that there might be all kinds of evidence.
sentences.zh: 问题在于可能会留下各种证据。

sentences.en: They don't really want the gunpowder to be found, because then the lead might go back to Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 他们其实不想让火药被发现，因为那样线索可能会顺藤摸瓜找到博思韦尔头上。

sentences.en: So they think,
sentences.zh: 所以他们想：

sentences.en: Oh, well, let's just blow it up anyway.
sentences.zh: “哦，好吧，不管怎样还是把它炸了吧。”

sentences.en: So that's what they do.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就这样做了。

sentences.en: And the fact that you have this kind of the chair and the rope and everything in the garden and the explosion is what has made it such
sentences.zh: 花园里留有椅子、绳子以及爆炸等种种迹象，正是这一点让它成为了一个如此

sentences.en: an enduring and tantalising mystery and why it's been so hard for people to solve.
sentences.zh: 经久不衰且扑朔迷离的谜团，也让人们如此难以破解。

sentences.en: But I think that that solution that Guy gives in his book, I mean, it seems to me the likeliest explanation for what actually happened.
sentences.zh: 但我认为盖伊在他的书中给出的那个解决方案，在我看来是对所发生事情最可能的解释。

sentences.en: So it's not a ritualistic killing, and it's not been designed that way.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一场仪式性的谋杀，它也不是被设计成那样的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It's just a result of him having tried to escape and this bloke Kerr kind of finding him.
sentences.zh: 这只是他试图逃跑而这家伙克尔正好找到了他所导致的后果。

sentences.en: So they strangled him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们勒死了他。

sentences.en: Why didn't they just stab him?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不直接捅死他？

sentences.en: That had worked with Rizzio.
sentences.zh: 对付里齐奥时那招挺管用的。

sentences.en: Why the strangulation?
sentences.zh: 为什么要用勒死的？

sentences.en: That's my question.
sentences.zh: 这是我的疑问。

sentences.en: I suppose to make his death seem as mysterious as possible, to kind of throw people off the scent.
sentences.zh: 我猜是为了让他的死显得尽可能神秘，好以此转移人们的视线。

sentences.en: And also you just want to mix things up a bit, don't you?
sentences.zh: 而且你总归是想变换一下手法，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't want to just use the same method every time.
sentences.zh: 你总不能每次都用同一招。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: They've already done the whole stabbing stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们已经用过捅刀子那一套了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Try something different.
sentences.zh: 尝试点新鲜的。

sentences.en: I mean, what would be brilliant if they'd had kind of 56 stab wounds like with Rizzio, but yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果像对付里齐奥那样有56处刀伤的话那可就太厉害了，不过好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But no.
sentences.zh: 但并没有。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So a couple of questions that are still hanging.
sentences.zh: 那么还有几个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: Number one, is it plausible that as Elizabeth sort of suggested in that letter, that Mary had been looking through
sentences.zh: 第一，伊丽莎白在那封信中某种程度上暗示的那种说法是否合理，即玛丽曾对这一行径

sentences.en: her fingers at the deed that she, okay, maybe she didn't officially authorize it formally,
sentences.zh: 睁一只眼闭一只眼，好吧，也许她没有正式给予官方授权，

sentences.en: but maybe she kind of knew that it was in the air and she just gave them a little wink or she just, or she did nothing.
sentences.zh: 但也许她心里清楚这件事正在酝酿，她只是给他们使了个眼色，或者她什么也没做。

sentences.en: She knew it was coming, but she did nothing to stop it.
sentences.zh: 她知道事情要发生，但她没有采取任何措施去阻止。

sentences.en: Well, it's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And we know of someone who did exactly that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道确实有人这么做了。

sentences.en: And this is the Earl of Moray whom Maitland in a very suggestive prefiguring of Elizabeth's use of the same phrase
sentences.zh: 这就是莫雷伯爵，梅特兰曾对伊丽莎白在给玛丽的信中使用过相同的短语进行了极具暗示性的预示，

sentences.en: in her letter to Mary had correctly predicted that although he wouldn't participate in the plot against Darnley, he would look through his fingers at preparations for the murder.
sentences.zh: 他曾准确地预测到，尽管他不会参与针对达恩利的阴谋，但他会对谋杀的筹备工作睁一只眼闭一只眼。

sentences.en: So in other words, you know, he would give it a nod and a wink.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你知道的，他会默许并递个眼色。

sentences.en: Basically Moray knew what was going to happen and he didn't inform Mary.
sentences.zh: 基本上莫雷知道将要发生什么，但他没有通知玛丽。

sentences.en: And instead aware that things were coming to a head, he had absented himself from Edinburgh and retreated to his estate in Fife so that he could say, look, nothing to do
sentences.zh: 相反，由于意识到事情正走向白热化，他离开爱丁堡退回到他在法夫的庄园，这样他就可以说：“看，这跟我一点关系也没有，老兄。”

sentences.en: with me, mate.
sentences.zh: 老兄。

sentences.en: Mary, of course, by contrast, I mean, she spends the evening before Darnley's murder,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，玛丽当然是在达恩利被谋杀的前一天晚上，

sentences.en: you know, partying in a house that is absolutely packed with gunpowder, which seems to me a very
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在一栋塞满了火药的房子里聚会，在我看来，这可以说是

sentences.en: strong circumstantial piece of evidence that she knew nothing whatsoever of the crime.
sentences.zh: 一个非常有力的间接证据，证明她对这起犯罪一无所知。

sentences.en: And also there was a slight hint of amusement when you read Antonia Fraser's account of Mary's tender heart.
sentences.zh: 而且当你读到安东尼娅·弗雷泽对玛丽菩萨心肠的描述时，也有一丝滑稽的意味。

sentences.en: Such a kind person.
sentences.zh: 真是个善良的人。

sentences.en: You know, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得这很对。

sentences.en: And in fact, I mean, you know, from your perspective, I would imagine
sentences.zh: 事实上，从你的角度来看，我想象

sentences.en: that's part of the problem with Mary.
sentences.zh: 这正是玛丽的问题所在。

sentences.en: She is too tender hearted.
sentences.zh: 她太心慈手软了。

sentences.en: Don't play the game unless you're going to play it properly.
sentences.zh: 既然要玩就得玩真的，否则就别玩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's my take on history, generally.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这就是我对历史的看法。

sentences.en: I think the conspirators feel like you do.
sentences.zh: 我想阴谋者们的感受和你一样。

sentences.en: That's why they don't tell her.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们不告诉她。

sentences.en: That's why they don't even hint at it because they're worried that she might step in and say, no, you're not allowed to do this.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么他们甚至连暗示都不敢暗示，因为他们担心她可能会介入并说：“不，你们不准这么做。”

sentences.en: And I think also another key piece of evidence that Mary didn't do it is her evident panic when she is told that Darnley had been killed because she does
sentences.zh: 而且我认为另一个能够证明玛丽没有参与此事的关键证据是，当得知达恩利被杀时她流露出的明显惊恐，因为在我看来，她确实

sentences.en: genuinely, it seems to me, she's very, very worried that she had been the target.
sentences.zh: 发自内心地非常非常担心自己成了袭击的目标。

sentences.en: So as Guy puts it,
sentences.zh: 正如盖伊所说，

sentences.en: Mary was a good actress, but not this good.
sentences.zh: 玛丽是个好演员，但没好到这种程度。

sentences.en: So all of that, I think kind of adds up to absolve Mary of the crime.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些，我认为都足以洗脱玛丽的罪名。

sentences.en: But just to reiterate, the key piece of evidence, I think, is that the timing for her is terrible in relation to her negotiations with Elizabeth, because she has
sentences.zh: 但重申一下，我认为最关键的证据是，这起事件的时间点对她与伊丽莎白的谈判来说简直糟透了，因为她

sentences.en: everything to lose.
sentences.zh: 将失去一切。

sentences.en: And actually in the event she does, because that letter from Elizabeth, which we began this episode with, I mean, it's a warning shot across Mary's bows.
sentences.zh: 事实上她也确实失去了，因为我们这集节目开头提到的伊丽莎白的那封信，那是对玛丽的严厉警告。

sentences.en: It's saying essentially, you know, solve the crime, arraign those who are responsible for it, or else there's no way that you are going to be my heir.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是在说，要么破案，将罪魁祸首绳之以法，否则你绝无可能成为我的继承人。

sentences.en: Does Mary solve the crime?
sentences.zh: 玛丽破案了吗？

sentences.en: The answer, I guess, is no.
sentences.zh: 我想答案是没有。

sentences.en: And this is disastrous for Mary.
sentences.zh: 这对玛丽来说是灾难性的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And her failure to do that results, I mean, in her total ruin.
sentences.zh: 而她未能做到这一点，意味着她的彻底毁灭。

sentences.en: And that of course leads to the second puzzle, which is why doesn't she manage to solve the crime?
sentences.zh: 这当然引出了第二个谜团，那就是为什么她没能破案？

sentences.en: Because as we know, there are very detailed and effective investigations.
sentences.zh: 因为如我们所知，当时进行了非常详细且有效的调查。

sentences.en: You know, there are people from the Privy Council who are interviewing the old women and taking down their records.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，枢密院的人一直在采访老妇人并做记录。

sentences.en: There's a jury's report that's gone to Cecil.
sentences.zh: 有一份陪审团的报告已经呈交给了塞西尔。

sentences.en: Why aren't these being collated and publicised rather than, as actually happens, being suppressed and in lots of cases completely forgotten?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些没有被整理并公之于众，反而在现实中被压制，甚至在很多情况下被彻底遗忘呢？

sentences.en: And the answer, again, I think is pretty obvious.
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为答案相当明显。

sentences.en: It's because those who commissioned these reports had every interest in suppressing them.
sentences.zh: 那是因为委托撰写这些报告的人有着充分的动机去将其压制。

sentences.en: Because the Privy
sentences.zh: 因为枢密院

sentences.en: Council, I mean, is absolutely full of people who had actually been responsible for Darnley's murder.
sentences.zh: 里到处都是真正应当为达恩利之死负责的人。

sentences.en: So, Bothwell, Morton, Maitland.
sentences.zh: 也就是博思韦尔、莫顿、梅特兰。

sentences.en: And of those three, Bothwell, Morton, Maitland, two in particular have a real reason to lie low and allow the rumour to do its work.
sentences.zh: 在这三个人（博思韦尔、莫顿、梅特兰）中，有两个人尤其有充分的理由保持低调，任由谣言四处流传。

sentences.en: Because one of those three is being fingered for the crime.
sentences.zh: 因为这三个人中有人正被指控为凶手。

sentences.en: And so the other two can say, well, you know, let's lie low and let him take the blame.
sentences.zh: 所以另外两人就可以说：“好吧，我们保持低调，让他来背锅吧。”

sentences.en: And the person who is being fingered for it is Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 而成为众矢之的、被指控为凶手的人正是博斯韦尔。

sentences.en: And accusations against Bothwell are starting to be laid within a week of Darnley's murder by his father, the Earl of Lennox.
sentences.zh: 就在达利遇害后的一周内，他的父亲伦诺克斯伯爵便开始指控博斯韦尔。

sentences.en: Placards and graffiti and cartoons start to appear across the streets of Edinburgh, charging Bothwell directly with the murder.
sentences.zh: 爱丁堡的街头开始出现标语、涂鸦和漫画，直接指控博斯韦尔谋杀。

sentences.en: Kind of caricatures of Bothwell start appearing on buildings and they have the label, here is the murder of the king.
sentences.zh: 建筑物上开始出现各种博斯韦尔的讽刺画，上面写着：这就是国王的谋杀者。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is very bad news for Bothwell, but it is also very, very bad news for Mary because rumours have
sentences.zh: 当然，这对于博斯韦尔来说是非常糟糕的消息，但对于玛丽而言也是极其糟糕的，因为有传言

sentences.en: been swirling throughout Scotland long before Darnley's murder that Mary has got a real crush on Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 早在达利遇害之前很久就在苏格兰流传开来，称玛丽对博斯韦尔动了真情。

sentences.en: And some of the evidence for this is bogus.
sentences.zh: 其中一些证据是伪造的。

sentences.en: So, for instance, the story that she had ridden alone to the hermitage when Bothwell had been stabbed, that wasn't true.
sentences.zh: 例如，关于博斯韦尔被刺伤时她独自骑马去隐修院的故事，并非事实。

sentences.en: But the fact the story was told is suggestive of how the trend of gossip is going.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事流传本身，就暗示了流言蜚语的发展方向。

sentences.en: And some of the stories are true.
sentences.zh: 而且有些故事确实是真的。

sentences.en: So, for instance, Mary had given Bothwell a spectacular blue suit at the christening and she had kind of
sentences.zh: 比如，在洗礼仪式上，玛丽曾送给博斯韦尔一套极为显眼的蓝色西装，她甚至

sentences.en: basically employed Bothwell to take the place of Darnley, her husband, who had refused to attend.
sentences.zh: 基本上让博斯韦尔取代了拒绝出席的丈夫达利的位置。

sentences.en: So, you can kind of see how these rumours, they have legs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你大概能看出这些传言为什么会越传越广。

sentences.en: And because of that, it doesn't take long for graffiti to start appearing on the walls of Edinburgh, charging that not only is Bothwell guilty
sentences.zh: 正因如此，没过多久，爱丁堡的墙上就开始出现涂鸦，指控不仅博斯韦尔

sentences.en: of Darnley's murder, but Mary is as well.
sentences.zh: 对达利的谋杀负有罪责，玛丽也同样难辞其咎。

sentences.en: And what about the English dimension to this, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，这其中英国方面的因素又该怎么看呢？

sentences.en: Because we started the whole episode with
sentences.zh: 因为我们在这一集的开头

sentences.en: Elizabeth the first letter.
sentences.zh: 就提到了伊丽莎白一世的信件。

sentences.en: What about Elizabeth and her chief minister, Cecil?
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白和她的内阁大臣塞西尔对此怎么看？

sentences.en: What do they make of all this?
sentences.zh: 他们对这一切作何感想？

sentences.en: Are they preparing to use this against Mary effectively, sort of cynically?
sentences.zh: 他们是否准备好利用这一点来对付玛丽，采取那种冷酷算计的态度？

sentences.en: Cecil, definitely.
sentences.zh: 塞西尔绝对是这样的。

sentences.en: We've been talking throughout this series how Cecil is Mary's great hidden enemy.
sentences.zh: 我们在整个系列节目中一直在谈论，塞西尔是玛丽最大的隐形敌人。

sentences.en: He's actively working to stop Mary succeeding to the English throne, but also he's pretty keen on toppling Mary from her own throne.
sentences.zh: 他不仅积极致力于阻止玛丽继承英国王位，而且还非常热衷于将玛丽从她自己的王位上推翻。

sentences.en: And so, he sees a huge opportunity here.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在这里看到了一个巨大的机会。

sentences.en: Why on earth would he publish anything that might help to absolve Mary?
sentences.zh: 他怎么可能会发表任何可能有助于玛丽洗脱罪名的话呢？

sentences.en: And I think definitely he is kind of pouring poison into Elizabeth's ear.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他绝对是在伊丽莎白耳边不断进谗言。

sentences.en: So, remember that phrase, looking through fingers, that Maitland had applied to Moray and that Elizabeth writes in her letter to Mary.
sentences.zh: 还记得那个词吗——梅特兰曾用来形容墨累、而伊丽莎白在写给玛丽的信中也用过的“隔岸观火”。

sentences.en: I think it's very easy to imagine Cecil having dropped precisely that phrase into conversation with Elizabeth and Elizabeth then using it herself in her letter.
sentences.zh: 我完全可以想象，正是塞西尔在与伊丽莎白的交谈中无意间说出了这个词，随后伊丽莎白便将其用在了自己的信中。

sentences.en: And then there is that anonymous traitor whom Elizabeth referred to in her letter comparing him to the minister of Satan.
sentences.zh: 还有伊丽莎白在信中提到的那个匿名叛徒，她将其比作撒旦的仆从。

sentences.en: She doesn't need to name him because it's so self-evidently Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 她根本不需要指名道姓，因为这显然就是在指博斯韦尔。

sentences.en: Now, you ask, does Elizabeth, like Cecil, want to see Mary ruined?
sentences.zh: 现在你会问，伊丽莎白是否和塞西尔一样，想要看到玛丽身败名裂？

sentences.en: No, she absolutely doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，她绝对不想。

sentences.en: Quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反。

sentences.en: So, just to quote that letter again, I exhort you, I counsel you, and I beseech you to take this thing so much to heart that you will not fear to touch
sentences.zh: 再引用一下那封信的原话：“我劝诫你，我奉劝你，我恳求你，务必将此事铭记于心，以至于你不会害怕去触及

sentences.en: even him whom you have nearest to you if the thing touches him.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是你最亲近的人，如果此事牵涉到他的话。”

sentences.en: What Elizabeth's trying to do is to help Mary safeguard her throne and not allow her reputation to be torched by this devastating
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白极力想要做的是，帮助玛丽保住她的王位，不让她的名誉被这铺天盖地、

sentences.en: accumulation of hostile rumour, of which two rumours in particular are the most lethal.
sentences.zh: 最具毁灭性的敌意传闻彻底摧毁，其中有两个传闻尤为致命。

sentences.en: One, that she had joined with Bothwell in the plot to murder Darnley.
sentences.zh: 第一，她与博斯韦尔串通谋害了达利。

sentences.en: And secondly, that she had done this out of an adulterous passion for Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 第二，她这样做是出于对博斯韦尔的通奸之情。

sentences.en: And so, Elizabeth is saying, for God's sake, you know, have nothing to do with Bothwell, arraign him, convict him, execute him.
sentences.zh: 所以伊丽莎白是在说，看在上帝的份上，你知道的，离博斯韦尔远点，控告他、定他的罪、处决他。

sentences.en: But the big question is, of course, will Mary listen to this self-evidently excellent advice?
sentences.zh: 但最大的问题当然是，玛丽会听取这个显而易见极其高明的建议吗？

sentences.en: Well, Mary has a history in this series of making very poor decisions.
